**1 — Scene:** Pizza with a leafy salad, olives, broccoli and cooked cherry tomatoes.

**2 — Vessel:** A roughly 26 cm square dinner plate. Allowing for rounded corners and perspective, I’ll use a 26 cm circular-equivalent area: 3.14 × 13² ≈ **530 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Cheese-and-tomato pizza, mixed salad leaves, black olives, broccoli, cherry tomatoes, and a light visible oil coating on the vegetables/salad. Pizza toppings are included in the pizza estimate.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pizza | 27% | 143 cm² × 1.5 cm = 215 ml | 0.9 | 193 g | 260 | 502 |
| Mixed leaves | 22% | 117 cm² × 2 cm = 234 ml | 0.15 | 35 g | 20 | 7 |
| Broccoli | 10% | 53 cm² × 2.8 cm = 148 ml | 0.55 | 82 g | 35 | 29 |
| Cherry tomatoes | 8% | 42 cm² × 1.8 cm = 76 ml | 0.65 | 50 g | 22 | 11 |
| Black olives | 1% | 5.3 cm² × 1.6 cm = 8.5 ml | 0.7 | 6 g | 145 | 9 |
| Oil coating | Overlay* | Approximately 5 ml | 1.0 | 5 g | 884 | 44 |

Food occupies approximately **68%** of the plate. *Oil coats existing food, so it adds no separate footprint.*

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **371 g and 602 kcal** is plausible for the visible pizza portion and modest vegetable sides. Pizza thickness and the oil quantity are the main uncertainties.
